transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining me. As you know, we're looking at authorizing a new eighth-grade makerspace program for the spring semester. The draft calls for 24 students meeting twice weekly, with soldering stations, hand tools, a laser cutter, and cloud-based CAD files, all under the supervision of one STEM teacher. Before I make a final decision, I'd like to hear from each of you on the implementation details relevant to your areas. Let's start with you, STEM teacher — can you walk me through how you'd plan to supervise 24 students with this equipment?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Before I address supervision, I need to share the findings from my room-safety review, which I completed this week. The review found that the makerspace may enroll no more than 16 students, and any session using soldering stations with more than 12 students requires two supervising adults. The draft program form still shows the original numbers — 24 students and one supervisor — but those will need to be revised to comply with the safety review.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share an important health finding before we proceed. My review of the participating students' health records identified one student with a documented severe nickel allergy. That student may only participate when the program uses nickel-free components, and I must approve the materials list before each session. I should also note that this health-record review has not yet been added to the program file.
transcript.speaker: A3
